`R: Reload Defeat all enemies`
- Start 0.5 seconds of damage invulnerability.
During the 0.5-second invulnerability period:
The per-frame damage limit is independent of the 0.5-second invulnerability duration.

before: If a Chaser remains in contact after the 0.8-second invulnerability expires, it may damage the player again.
after: If a Chaser remains in contact after the 0.5-second invulnerability expires, it may damage the player again.
A new valid damage event starts a new 0.5-second invulnerability period.
- Damage-invulnerability duration: 0.5 seconds when activated

before: 5. Process player damage from recorded enemy-bullet hits and Chaser contact, allowing at most 1 HP loss for the frame.
6. Update Reload, damage-invulnerability, player flashing, and enemy hit-highlight timers.
after: 5. Process player damage from recorded enemy-bullet hits and Chaser contact, allowing at most 1 HP loss for the frame. Any valid damage starts 0.5 seconds of damage invulnerability.
6. Update Reload, the 0.5-second damage-invulnerability timer, player flashing, and enemy hit-highlight timers.
During Step 5:
- If damage invulnerability is already active, Chaser contact cannot reduce HP.
- Enemy-bullet collisions cannot reduce HP, but those bullets are still removed.
- If invulnerability is inactive and multiple valid damage sources occur in the same frame, only one can decrease HP.
- After that valid damage, the 0.5-second invulnerability period begins.
- The damage-invulnerability timer to inactive.

before: Valid player damage immediately decreases HP by 1 and starts the 0.8-second flashing invulnerability period.
The player can lose at most 1 HP in a single frame.
after: Valid player damage immediately decreases HP by 1 and starts a 0.5-second flashing invulnerability period.
During this 0.5-second period:
- Chaser contact cannot cause additional HP loss.
- Enemy bullets cannot cause additional HP loss.
- Enemy bullets that collide still disappear.
The player can lose at most 1 HP in a single frame regardless of the invulnerability duration.
If a Chaser remains in contact when the 0.5-second invulnerability period expires, it may damage the player again.
